_comment: First-host probes for road-to-skills-that-arrive-when-called 0.2, in the row shape of host-injection-effect.json (validated by recordProblems in src/scripts/_lib/injection_effect.ts) plus a host and an expiry. An `observed-*` row needs host_version, transcript and date; the transcripts are machine-local session files under ~/.claude/projects and are named, not committed. Every probe skill was named zz-arrival-probe-*, lived under the user skills root only for the probe, and was removed afterwards. Phase 4 of the roadmap is gated on rows (a) and (b) here being observed-true.

a-same-turn-pickup-symlink.reason: Probe (a), symlink. A `claude -p` session ran `ln -s` into ~/.claude/skills and then called the Skill tool by name in the same turn. In the first session the call returned `Launching skill: zz-arrival-probe-a2` on the first attempt. In the second (2eff55cb) the first call returned `Unknown skill: zz-arrival-probe-d1`, the skill appeared in the listing right after, and one retry launched it. So pickup is same-turn but races the directory watcher: a materialiser must expect one miss and retry once, never assume the first call lands. A second, unrelated live session on the same machine also received both new skills in its listing mid-turn.

a-same-turn-pickup-copy.reason: Probe (a), copy. Both attempts to `cp -R` a skill folder into ~/.claude/skills were refused by the host's auto-mode permission classifier (once inside the probe session, once from the lane that ran the probes), so the copy case was never written. Needs a run with a permission rule for that copy, or the owner running it.

b-removed-skill-second-session.reason: Probe (b). Listing: an entry is never withdrawn by a removal — both a resumed session and a second live session kept listing the removed skill. Already-loaded body: it stays in the conversation (the resumed session restated the token without a tool call). Invocation differs by process: a RESUMED session (new process) answered `Unknown skill: zz-arrival-probe-a2` after the symlink was removed although its target still existed; a session that stayed LIVE throughout still launched a skill whose symlink had been removed while the target folder existed, and answered `Unknown skill` only once the target was gone too. So removing the entry does not stop a live session that already resolved it, and removing the content does — the shape step 4.4's lease must hold for.

c-session-start-reload-flag.reason: Probe (c). The flag is documented: `hookSpecificOutput.reloadSkills: true` on SessionStart makes the host re-scan the skill and command directories after SessionStart hooks complete, because discovery otherwise runs before they finish (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, read 2026-10-18). Not observed: preparing a SessionStart hook that installs a skill was refused by the host's auto-mode permission classifier in the lane that ran (a), (b) and (d).

d-context-large.reason: Probe (d). A skill carrying the retired package value `context: large` launched inline: no subagent or forked context was started, the body arrived as a message in the invoking conversation, and the model could see earlier turns including a canary word. The host neither errors on the unknown value nor forks on it, so before 1.1 the key was silently inert, not harmful — and no skill could have forked while it held the key.

e-name-only-listing.reason: Probe (e), read from the search roadmap's 0.1 evidence file rather than re-probed, as the step asks: `skillOverrides: name-only` keeps the listing entry without its description while invocation by the Skill tool and by `/name` both still work. The transcript pointer is that file, which carries the session pointers of the original runs.
